title: Fast two-dimensional tensor-network contraction via subspace iteration
abstract: The corner transfer matrix renormalization group (CTMRG) is one of the standard contraction methods for infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS), but its computational cost is dominated by repeated truncated singular value decompositions (SVDs). We introduce subspace-iteration CTMRG (SI-CTMRG), a QR-based projector construction that replaces each large-matrix SVD with an SVD of a much smaller matrix. The resulting algorithm shifts the dominant cost from decompositions to tensor contractions, making it highly suited to GPU acceleration and yielding speedups of up to two orders of magnitude over standard CTMRG. We demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the method for the triangular-lattice Heisenberg antiferromagnet, reaching state-of-the-art iPEPS results on a single H100 GPU in approximately 10 hours of computation.
summary: This paper introduces Subspace Iteration CTMRG (SI-CTMRG) to drastically improve the computational efficiency of calculating properties on infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS). By replacing costly large-matrix Singular Value Decompositions with smaller, iterative updates, the method shifts the bottleneck to GPU-friendly tensor contractions. It successfully applies this technique to the triangular Heisenberg antiferromagnet, achieving state-of-the-art results much faster than previous methods.
main_problem: The primary goal is to improve the computational efficiency of calculating observables on infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) by accelerating the Corner Transfer Matrix Renormalization Group (CTMRG) contraction step.
main_result: The proposed SI-CTMRG method shifts the dominant cost from computationally expensive SVDs to tensor contractions, yielding significant speedups (up to two orders of magnitude) and achieving state-of-the-art results for the triangular Heisenberg antiferromagnet on modern GPUs.
method: It introduces Subspace Iteration CTMRG (SI-CTMRG), a QR-based projector construction that replaces large-matrix SVDs with smaller, iterative updates followed by a small SVD. This makes the method highly suitable for GPU acceleration and fixed-point automatic differentiation.
model_or_system: The method is demonstrated on two-dimensional quantum lattice systems, specifically using the spin-1/2 nearest-neighbor Heisenberg antiferromagnet Hamiltonian on the triangular lattice, which exhibits 120-degree magnetic order.
key_observables: Energy per site ($e$), local magnetic moment ($m$), and correlation length ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Bond dimension ($\chi$), oversampling parameter ($p$), and computational time/GPU resources (H100).
main_assumptions: The standard CTMRG bottleneck is the cubic scaling of large-matrix SVDs, which SI-CTMRG circumvents by using subspace iteration updates.
figures_summary: Figures compare energy convergence and time per step between standard CTMRG and SI-CTMRG; Figure 3 shows linear extrapolation plots for ground state properties ($e$ vs $1/\xi^{*3}$) comparing results to other methods.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of standard CTMRG, details the novel SI-CTMRG algorithm using QR decomposition and subspace iteration, applies it to the triangular Heisenberg model, validates its efficiency via speedup comparisons, and finally presents extrapolated ground state properties consistent across different ansatz sizes.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter models, the core contribution is a highly efficient numerical technique for tensor network contractions (iPEPS/CTMRG), which has broad applicability in simulating quantum many-body systems beyond standard DMRG limits.
